# I. Overview {#i.-overview}

## 1\. User Requirements {#1.-user-requirements}

### 1.1 Actors {#1.1-actors}

| \# | Actor | Description |
| ----- | :---- | :---- |
| 1 | Guest |  |
| 2 | Admin | A system administrator who manages user accounts, roles, permissions, and global system settings within the LMS.  |
| 3 | Instructor | A content creator who develops courses, uploads learning materials, designs multiple-choice quizzes, manages coupons, interacts with student reviews, and tracks personal course revenue.  |
| 4 | Learner  | A user who browses and purchases courses, manages their shopping cart and orders, accesses video lectures and materials, submits feedback, and tracks their study schedules.  |
| 5 | Manager  | A system administrator who manages instructor requests, reviews and approves courses, manages categories, monitors system revenue, and moderates reported student feedback.  |
| 6 | Mail Service | An external email service integrated with the LMS to send notifications, password recovery emails, and system announcements.  |

#### *a. Diagram(s)*

#### *b. Descriptions*

| ID | Feature | Use Case | Use Case Description |
| ----- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **GUEST / REGISTERED USER** |  |  |  |
| UC-01 | Registered User | Register account | Create a new account by providing personal information and login credentials, or by signing up using a Google (Gmail) account. |
| UC-02 | Registered User | Login | Log into the system to access role-specific pages and functions. |
| UC-03 | Registered User | Forgot password | Request OTP by email and reset password. |
| UC-04 | Registered User | Logout | Register User can logout from the system. |

| UC-06 | User Management | View Detail User | Allow Admin, Instructor ,Learner to view user account details: Profile, Email, Role, Status, Created date. |
| UC-07 | User Management | Edit User | Allow Admin, Instructor ,Learner to update user information, change user role, lock/unlock user, reset password, delete user. |

| UC-12 | Instructor-request  Management | View Detail Instructor Request | Allow Manager to view instructor request details: Profile, CV, Certificate, Description. |
| UC-13 | Instructor-request  Management | Edit Instructor Request | Allow Manager to approve instructor, reject instructor, block instructor. |
| UC-14 | Category Management | Add Category | Allow Manager to add a new category. |
| UC-15 | Category Management | List Categories | Allow Manager to view the list of categories. |
| UC-16 | Category Management | View Detail Category | Allow Manager to view category details: Category Name, Description, Total Courses, Status. |
| UC-17 | Category Management | Edit Category | Allow Manager to update category, delete category. |
| UC-18 | Course Management | Edit Course | Allow Manager to approve course, reject course, hide course and instructor can add material , video in course |
| UC-19 | Revenue Management | View Revenue Dashboard | Allow Manager to view the system revenue dashboard. |
| UC-20 | Revenue Management | List Transactions | Allow Manager to view the list of transactions. |
| UC-21 | Feedback Moderation | List Reported Feedbacks | Allow Manager to view the list of reported feedbacks. |
| UC-22 | Feedback Moderation | View Detail Reported Feedback | Allow Manager to view reported feedback details. |
| UC-23 | Feedback Moderation | Edit Feedback Status | Allow Manager to hide feedback, delete feedback, mark feedback as violation. |
| **INSTRUCTOR** |  |  |  |
| UC-24 | Course Management | Create Course | Allows the instructor to create a new course with basic information (title, category, price) and save it as a draft. |
| UC-25 | Material Management | Create Material | Allows the instuctor to upload learning materials (videos, PDFs, slides) to their media library. |
| UC-26 | Material Management | List Materials | Allows the instructor to view all uploaded files along with their sizes, formats, and usage status. |
| UC-27 | Material Management | View Material Detail | Allows the instructor to preview material content and view its technical specifications. |
| UC-28 | Material Management | Edit Material | Allows the instructor to replace an existing material file, update its name, or delete it from the library. |
| UC-29 | Quiz Management | Create Quiz | Allows the instructor to initialize a new multiple-choice quiz, setting its time limit, pass mark, and question bank. |
| UC-30 | Quiz Management | List Quiz | Allows the instructor to view all created quizzes and see which lessons they are assigned to. |
| UC-31 | Quiz Management | View Quiz Detail | Allows the instructor to view the questions, correct answers, and performance statistics of a quiz. |
| UC-32 | Quiz Management | Edit Quiz | Allows the instructor to modify quiz questions, update correct answers, or adjust test parameters. |
| UC-33 | Marketing Management | Create Coupon | Allows the instructor to generate a new promotional discount code with usage limits and expiry dates. |
| UC-34 | Marketing Management | List Coupons | Allows the instructor to view all active and expired coupons along with their redemption counts. |
| UC-35 | Marketing Management | Edit Coupon | Allows the instructor to modify the limits or expiry date of an active coupon, or disable it entirely. |
| UC-36 | Revenue Management | View Detail Transaction | Allow Manager, Instrcutor to view transaction details: Student, Purchased Courses, Payment Amount, Payment Status, Transaction Date. |
| **LEARNER** |  |  |  |
| UC-37 | Course Management | List Courses | Allow Manager, Leaner , instructor to view the list of courses. |
| UC-38 | Course Management | View Detail Course | Allow Manager, Leaner, instructor to view course details: Thumbnail, Description, Lessons, Materials, Instructor, Price, Status. |
| UC-39 | Cart Management | View Cart | Allow Learner to view the items currently in their shopping cart. (Note: A new cart is only created when an item is added, otherwise it shows as empty). |
| UC-40 | Cart Management | Edit Cart | Allow Learner to update or remove courses in their shopping cart before purchasing. |
| UC-41 | Order Management | Create Order | Allow Learner to proceed to checkout and create a new order from the items in their cart. |
| UC-42 | Order Management | Edit Order | Allow Learner to modify the selected courses within an order before payment confirmation. |
| UC-43 | Order Management | List Orders | Allow Learner to view a list of all their orders, including pending, active, and completed ones. |
| UC-44 | Order Management | View Order Details | Allow Learner to view specific details of an order, including the exact courses purchased. |
| UC-45 | Course Learning | List Lesson | Allow Learner to browse the list of video lectures available within an enrolled course. |
| UC-46 | Course Learning | View Lesson Content | Allow Learner to watch individual video lectures and access the lesson content. |
| UC-47 | Course Learning | List Materials | Allow Learner to see the list of downloadable learning materials attached to the course. |
| UC-48 | Course Learning | View Material Details | Allow Learner to view details and download specific study documents/materials. |
| **UC-49** | Feedback System | Create Feedback | Allow Learner to submit reviews and feedback after experiencing a course. |
| **UC-50** | Feedback System | Edit Feedback | Allow Learner to update or delete their own submitted feedback. |
| **UC-51** | Feedback System | List Feedbacks | Allow Learner,Instructor to view the list of feedback and reviews from other students. |

### 2.4 Non-UI Functions {#2.4-non-ui-functions}

| \# | Feature | System Function | Description |
| :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: |
| 1 | Authentication | Password Hashing | Automatically encrypts user passwords using a secure algorithm (e.g., BCrypt) before storing them in the database. |
| 2 | Payment Gateway Integration | Asynchronous Payment Callback & IPN Handling | Listens for secure asynchronous notifications (Instant Payment Notification / IPN) from payment gateways (e.g., VNPay, PayPal, Stripe) to verify transaction status and automatically update order status to "Completed". |
| 3 | Order Management | Pending Order Auto-Expiration Job | A background cron job that periodically checks the database and automatically cancels/expires pending orders after 15 minutes of inactivity, releasing reserved resources. |
| 4 | Material Management | Azure Storage & Media Processing | Uploads course documents and raw video files to Azure Blob Storage, triggers Azure Media Services to compress and transcode videos into adaptive streaming formats (e.g., HLS/DASH) at multiple resolutions, and delivers them via Azure CDN to optimize streaming performance. |
| 5 | Study Schedule | Daily Schedule Reminder & Notification Service | A daily background job that compiles enrolled learners' scheduled tasks, checks their progress, and triggers personalized email digests or notifications regarding their daily study schedules. |
| 6 | Marketing Management | Coupon Validation & Auto-Expiration Engine | Automatically validates coupon applicability during checkout (checking limits and expiry dates) and dynamically marks coupons as "Expired" or "Inactive" once limits or dates are reached. |
| 7 | Mail Service | Transactional & Broadcast Email Dispatcher | Asynchronously queues and dispatches transactional emails (e.g., registration OTPs, order receipts, password recovery links) and course approval status notifications. |
| 8 | Course Progress | Watch-Time Tracker & Course Progress Aggregator | Periodically logs Learner video playback timestamps, verifies if 90% threshold is met to mark lesson "Completed", and recalculates overall course progress percentage. |
| 9 | Revenue Management | Monthly Instructor Payout & Analytics Aggregation | An automated monthly job that calculates net transaction revenues, deducts platform commission, and generates revenue summaries for instructors and manager dashboards. |

# II. Requirement Specifications {#ii.-requirement-specifications}

## 1\. \<\<Feature Name\>\> {#1.-<<feature-name>>}

### 1.1 \<\<UseCaseCode\_UC Name\>\> {#1.1-<<usecasecode_uc-name>>}

#### *a. Functionalities*

Provide the functional description for the use cases using the template/guides below  
**Functional Description Template**

| UC ID and Name: | UC-21: Create Course |  |  |
| ----: | :---- | ----: | :---- |
| Created By: | Anhtq | Date Created: | 25/May/2026 |
| Primary Actor: | Instructor | Secondary Actors: | Manager |
| Trigger: | The Instructor selects the “Create Course” option from the Course Management dashboard.  |  |  |
| Description: | This use case allows an Instructor to create a new course by entering basic information such as title, category, and price, and saving it as a draft before publishing it later.  |  |  |
| Preconditions: | The Instructor has successfully logged into the system. The Instructor has permission to create a course. The Course Management module is available and functioning. |  |  |
| Postconditions: | A new course is created and stored in the system. The course status is set to **Draft**. The course is not visible to learners yet. |  |  |
| Normal Flow: | The Instructor logs into the system. The Instructor navigates to the Course Management section. The Instructor selects “Create Course”. The system displays the course creation form. The Instructor enters course information (title, category, price). The Instructor clicks “Save Draft”. The system validates the input data. The system saves the course into the database with status “Draft”. The system displays a success message confirming course creation. |  |  |
| Alternative Flows: |   **AF1: Missing or invalid input data** The system displays validation error messages. The Instructor is required to correct the input and resubmit.   **AF2: Save as draft for later editing** The Instructor can later access the draft course from the course list and continue editing. |  |  |
| Exceptions: | E1: Database error occurs while saving → system displays “Save failed, please try again.” E2: Network connection failure → the system cannot complete the request. E3: Invalid data (e.g., negative price, empty title). |  |  |
| Priority: | High (Medium, Low), Must Have (Should Have, Could Have),.. |  |  |
| Frequency of Use: | High (Instructors frequently create new courses)  |  |  |
| Business Rules: | The course price must be greater than or equal to 0\. The title field is mandatory and cannot be empty. A newly created course must default to **Draft** status. Instructors can only create courses under their own account. |  |  |
| Other Information: | Future enhancements may include thumbnail upload, description, and video preview. Auto-save draft functionality may be supported. |  |  |
| Assumptions: | The Instructor role is already properly configured in the system. The database supports Draft and Published states. The Course Management module is stable and available. |  |  |

| UC ID and Name: | UC-21: Create Material |  |  |
| ----: | :---- | ----: | :---- |
| Created By: | Anhtq | Date Created: | 25/May/2026 |
| Primary Actor: | Instructor | Secondary Actors: | None |
| Trigger: | The Instructor selects the “Upload Material” option from the Material Management section or lesson detail page.  |  |  |
| Description: | This use case allows an Instructor to upload learning materials such as PDF files, slides, source code, or documents and attach them to a lesson.  |  |  |
| Preconditions: | 1\. The Instructor has successfully logged into the system. 2\. The Instructor owns the related course/lesson. 3\. The lesson already exists in the system. 4\. The Material Management module is available and functioning.  |  |  |
| Postconditions: | 1\. A new material is uploaded and stored in the system. 2\. The material is linked to the selected lesson. 3\. Learners enrolled in the course can access the material.  |  |  |
| Normal Flow: | 1\. The Instructor logs into the system. 2\. The Instructor navigates to Course Management. 3\. The Instructor selects a lesson. 4\. The Instructor clicks “Upload Material”. 5\. The system displays the material upload form. 6\. The Instructor selects a file and enters material information (file name, type). 7\. The Instructor submits the upload request. 8\. The system validates the file information. 9\. The system uploads and stores the file. 10\. The system creates a new material record in the database. 11\. The system displays a success message confirming material upload  |  |  |
| Alternative Flows: |  **AF1: Unsupported file format → The system displays a validation error. AF2: Instructor uploads a replacement file → The system updates the material information. AF3: Instructor uploads multiple materials sequentially.**  |  |  |
| Exceptions: | **E1:** File upload failed due to server error. **E2:** File size exceeds system limit. **E3:** Network connection failure during upload. **E4:** Database error while saving material information.  |  |  |
| Priority: | High – Must Have  |  |  |
| Frequency of Use: | High  |  |  |
| Business Rules: | 1\. A material must belong to a lesson. 2\. Only the course owner can upload materials. 3\. The uploaded file type must be supported by the system. 4\. File size must not exceed the configured limit.  Instructors can only create courses under their own account. |  |  |
| Other Information: | Future enhancements may support drag-and-drop upload, video materials, and cloud storage integration.  |  |  |
| Assumptions: | The related lesson already exists and the file storage service is available.  |  |  |

The system displays a success message confirming quiz creation.  |  |  |

| UC ID and Name: | UC-37: List Courses |  |  |
| ----: | :---- | ----: | :---- |
| Created By: | ThanhDH | Date Created: | 25/May/2026 |
| Primary Actor: | Learner, Instructor, Manager, Guest | Secondary Actors: | None |
| Trigger: | The user navigates to the "Courses" or "Course Catalog" page from the main header or dashboard. |  |  |
| Description: | Allows users (including unauthenticated guests) to browse, search, filter, and sort the list of courses available on the LMS platform. |  |  |
| Preconditions: | The course catalog database is active and online. |  |  |
| Postconditions: | The list of courses matching the search, filter, or sorting criteria is successfully displayed to the user. |  |  |
| Normal Flow: |  The user navigates to the Course Catalog page.  The system retrieves the list of active, published courses from the database. The system displays the courses in a card-based grid layout including:    Thumbnail, Title, Instructor Name, Rating (stars and value), Total Enrolled Learners, and Price. The user browses the courses. |  |  |
| Alternative Flows: | **AF1:  Search for Courses** 1\. The user enters keyword(s) in the search bar. 2\. The system filters the course list dynamically, matching the course title, description, or instructor name with the keywords. 3\. The system displays the matching results. **AF2:  Filter Courses by Category** 1\. The user selects a category (e.g., Development, Business, IT & Software) from the filter sidebar. 2\. The system filters and displays only the courses belonging to the selected category. **AF3:  Sort Courses**  1\. The user selects a sorting option (e.g., "Most Popular", "Highest Rated", "Price: Low to High", "Price: High to Low"). 2\. The system dynamically re-orders the displayed courses based on the chosen criterion.   |  |  |
| Exceptions: | **E1:  No Courses Found** 1\. The system detects that no courses match the search or filter criteria. 2\. The system displays a friendly message: "No courses found matching your criteria." and provides a "Reset Filters" button. **E2:  Database Connection Error** 1\. The system fails to retrieve course data from the database. 2\. The system displays an error: "Unable to load courses at the moment. Please try again later."  |  |  |
| Priority: | High  |  |  |
| Frequency of Use: | Very High. |  |  |
| Business Rules: | Unregistered Guests and Learners can only view courses that are in **Published** status. Instructors can view all of their own courses (including Draft, Pending Approval, Published, Hidden) but can only view Published courses from other instructors. Course listings must support pagination with a default limit of 12 courses per page. |  |  |
| Other Information: | 1\. Search queries must be sanitized to prevent injection attacks. 2\. Course listings must support smooth lazy-loading or standard pagination. |  |  |
| Assumptions: | The database contains active course data. Categories and settings are pre-configured. |  |  |

| ----: | :---- | ----: | :---- |

| Primary Actor: | Guest, Learner, Instructor, Manager | Secondary Actors: | Azure Blob Storage / Azure CDN |
| Trigger: | The user selects a specific course card from the Course Catalog, Cart, or Dashboard. |  |  |
| Description: | Allows users (including unauthenticated guests) to view detailed information about a specific course, including its thumbnail, full description, curriculum lessons, preview materials, instructor profile summary, price, and learner reviews. |  |  |
| Preconditions: | The course catalog database is active and online. |  |  |
| Postconditions: | The detailed page of the selected course is displayed containing comprehensive course attributes. |  |  |
| Normal Flow: |  The user clicks on a specific course from the list.  The system retrieves full course details from the database, including metadata, curriculum, and reviews.  The system checks the user's enrollment status for this course.  The system renders the Course Details page displaying: thumbnail, title, subtitle, full description, author summary, rating, student enrollment count, pricing, and curriculum.  The system displays a "Add to Cart" button (since the user is not enrolled). |  |  |
| Alternative Flows: | **AF1:  Instructor is the Owner** 1\.  At step 3, the system detects that the logged-in user is the Instructor who created the course. 2\. The system displays an "Edit Course" button and a preview mode of the course as it would appear to learners. **AF2:  Preview Free Lecture** 1\. The user scrolls to the curriculum section. 2\. The user clicks "Preview" next to a lecture marked as a free preview. 3\. The system retrieves the preview video from Azure CDN and streams it in a modal player. |  |  |
| Exceptions: | **E1:  Course Not Found** 1\. The system cannot find the course with the specified ID in the database. 2\. The system redirects the user to a "404 \- Course Not Found" page. **E2:  Course is Inactive/Hidden** 1\. The system detects the course is in Draft or Hidden status and the current user is not the owner or a manager. 2\. The system blocks access and displays: "This course is currently not available."  |  |  |
| Priority: | High  |  |  |
| Frequency of Use: | Very High. |  |  |
| Business Rules: | Unenrolled Learners and Guests cannot access the full learning materials or watch locked videos; they can only view the course overview, syllabus, and promotional previews. The course owner (Instructor) and Managers can view course details regardless of whether the course status is Draft, Pending Approval, Hidden, or Published. The system must dynamically verify the user's enrollment status upon page load to display the appropriate call-to-action button (e.g., "Add to Cart", "Start Learning", or "Edit Course"). |  |  |
| Other Information: | 1\. Social sharing buttons (Facebook, Twitter, LinkedIn) are supported. 2\. Curriculum content shows lock icons for paid/enrolled lectures. |  |  |
| Assumptions: | Course metadata, lessons, and reviews are fully populated in the database. |  |  |

| UC ID and Name: | UC-39: View Cart |  |  |
| ----: | :---- | ----: | :---- |
| Created By: | ThanhDH | Date Created: | 25/May/2026 |
| Primary Actor: | Learner | Secondary Actors: | None |
| Trigger: | The Learner clicks on the shopping cart icon in the main header. |  |  |
| Description: | Allows authenticated learners to view the list of courses they have added to their shopping cart before checking out. It displays item details, individual pricing, applicable coupon inputs, and the total order amount. |  |  |
| Preconditions: | PRE-1. The Learner is successfully logged into the LMS system. PRE-2. The cart database or session is active and accessible. |  |  |
| Postconditions: | POST-1. The shopping cart details are successfully displayed to the Learner. |  |  |
| Normal Flow: |  The Learner clicks the shopping cart icon.  The system retrieves the list of courses currently saved in the Learner's cart from the database or session.  The system checks if each course is still active and in Published status. The system will automatically group the courses in your shopping cart by instructor.  The system calculates the subtotal, system fees (if any), and the overall total price.  The system renders the Cart page displaying: course details (thumbnail, title, rating, instructor, original price), a promo code input box, the summary of pricing, and a "Checkout" button. |  |  |
| Alternative Flows: | **AF1: Cart is Empty** 1\. At step 2, the system detects that there are no courses in the Learner's cart. 2\. The system displays an empty cart state: "Your cart is empty." and provides a "Browse Courses" button. 3\. The "Proceed to Checkout" button is hidden or disabled. **AF2:  Remove Course from Cart** 1\. The Learner clicks the "Remove" or "Trash" icon next to a course in the cart list. 2\. The system deletes the selected course from the cart record. 3\. The system recalculates the subtotal and total price. 4\. The system dynamically updates the cart count in the header and refreshes the cart list. |  |  |
| Exceptions: | **\- Course Price or Status Changed** 1\. At step 3, the system detects that a course in the cart is no longer Published (e.g., Hidden or Draft) or its price has been modified by the instructor. 2\. The system updates the cart dynamically, removes any unavailable courses, applies the new price, and alerts the Learner: "Some items in your cart have changed status or pricing." |  |  |
| Priority: | High  |  |  |
| Frequency of Use: | High (frequently accessed during shopping flows). |  |  |
| Business Rules: | The shopping cart items for an authenticated Learner must be stored in the database so they persist across different devices and login sessions. The system must validate the availability and status of all courses in the cart upon page load. If a course is hidden, deleted, or already owned, it must be automatically removed from the cart. |  |  |
| Other Information: | 1\. The cart state persists across sessions if the user logs out and logs in again (saved in the database). |  |  |
| Assumptions: | The Learner has an active session. |  |  |

**Functional Description Contents**  
***Use Case ID and Name***

Give each use case a unique integer sequence number identifier. State a concise name for the use case that indicates the value the use case would provide to some user. Begin with an action verb, followed by an object.

***Author and Date Created***

Enter the name of the person who initially wrote this use case and the date it was written.

***Primary and Secondary Actors***

An actor is a person or other entity external to the software system being specified who interacts with the system and performs use cases to accomplish tasks. Different actors often correspond to different user classes, or roles, identified from the customer community that will use the product. Name the primary actor that will be initiating this use case and any other secondary actors who will participate in completing execution of the use case.

***Trigger***

Identify the business event, system event, or user action that initiates the use case. This trigger alerts the system that it should begin testing the preconditions for the use case so it can judge whether to proceed with execution.

***Description***

Provide a brief description of the reason for and outcome of this use case, or a high-level description of the sequence of actions and the outcome of executing the use case.

***Preconditions***

List any activities that must take place, or any conditions that must be true, before the use case can be started. The system must be able to test each precondition. Number each precondition. Example: PRE-1: User’s identity has been authenticated.

***Postconditions***

Describe the state of the system at the successful conclusion of the use case execution. Label each postcondition in the form POST-X, where X is a sequence number. Example: POST-1: Price of item in the database has been updated with the new value.

***Normal Flow***

Provide a description of the user actions and corresponding system responses that will take place during execution of the use case under normal, expected conditions. This dialog sequence will ultimately lead to accomplishing the goal stated in the use case name and description. Show a numbered list of actions performed by the actor, alternating with responses provided by the system. The normal flow is numbered “X.0”, where “X” is the Use Case ID.

***Alternative Flows***

Document other successful usage scenarios that can take place within this use case. State the alternative flow, and describe any differences in the sequence of steps that take place. Number each alternative flow in the form “X.Y”, where “X” is the Use Case ID and Y is a sequence number for the alternative flow. For example, “5.3” would indicate the third alternative flow for use case number 5\. Indicate where each alternative flow would branch off from the normal flow, and if pertinent, where it would rejoin the normal flow.

***Exceptions***

Describe any anticipated error conditions that could occur during execution of the use case and how the system is to respond to those conditions. Number each alternative flow in the form “X.Y.EZ”, where “X” is the Use Case ID, Y indicates the normal (0) or alternative (\>0) flow during which this exception could take place, “E” indicates an exception, and “Z” is a sequence number for the exceptions. For example “5.0.E2” would indicate the second exception for the normal flow for use case number 5\. Indicate where in the normal (or an alternative) flow each exception could occur.

***Priority***

Indicate the relative priority of implementing the functionality required to allow this use case to be executed. Use the same priority scheme as that used for the functional requirements.

***Frequency of Use***

Estimate the number of times this use case will be performed per some appropriate unit of time. This gives an early indicator of throughput, concurrent usage loads, and transaction capacity.

***Business Rules***

List any business rules that influence this use case. Don’t include the business rule text here, just its identifier so the reader can find it in another repository when needed.

***Other Information***

Identify any additional requirements, such as quality attributes, for the use case that may need to be addressed during design or implementation. Also list any associated functional requirements that aren’t a direct part of the use case flows but which a developer needs to know about. Describe what should happen if the use case execution fails for some unanticipated or systemic reason (e.g., loss of network connectivity, timeout). If the use case results in a durable state change in a database or the outside world, state whether the change is rolled back, completed correctly, partially completed with a known state, or left in an undetermined state as a result of the exception.

***Assumptions***

List any assumptions that were made regarding this use case or how it might execute.

## 3\. Create Order  {#3.-create-order}

### 3.1 UC-16\_Create Order  {#3.1-uc-16_create-order}

#### *a. Functional Description*

| ID and Name: | UC-16 Create Order  |  |  |
| ----: | :---- | ----: | :---- |
| Created By: | HoangCT | Date Created: | 25/5/2026 |
| Primary Actor: | Learner  | Secondary Actors: | Payment Gateway System (e.g., VNPay, PayPal, Stripe)  |
| Description: | Learner can proceed to checkout and create a new order from the courses currently in their shopping cart. The system validates the cart, applies discounts (if any), and creates an order record awaiting payment.  When creating an order, the system will separate the discount amount and discount code used and apply it to each corresponding course detail line (order\_items), instead of saving the discount for the entire large order. |  |  |
| Trigger: | Learner clicks the "Checkout" or "Proceed to Payment" button from the Cart page.  |  |  |
| Preconditions: | PRE-1. Learner is logged into the E-learning system.  PRE-2. Learner has at least one valid course in their shopping cart.  |  |  |
| Postconditions: | POST-1. A new order record is created successfully.  POST-2. Order status is set to "Successful Payment".  POST-3. If the total amount is 0 (free course), the order status is updated to "Completed" and Learner is enrolled immediately.  |  |  |
| Normal Flow: |  Learner clicks "Checkout" from the shopping cart.  System displays the order summary including selected courses, subtotal, system fees, and total price.  Learner selects a preferred payment method.  Learner clicks "Confirm Order".  System validates the cart items (checks if courses are still active and not already owned).  System creates a new order record with "Pending Payment" status.  System saves the order data in the database.  System redirects the Learner to the selected Payment Gateway System. |  |  |
| Alternative Flows: | \- Apply Coupon Code 1\. Learner enters a promotional code before confirming the order. 2\. System validates the coupon code (usage limits, expiry date). 3\. System recalculates the final price based on the discount. 4\. Return to step 3 of the normal flow. \- Checkout with Free Courses 1\. System detects the total order value is $0. 2\. System skips step 8 of the normal flow. 3\. System updates order status to "Completed" and enrolls the Learner automatically. |  |  |
| Exceptions: | \- Course Already Owned 1\. System detects Learner already owns a course present in the cart. 2\. System informs Learner and automatically removes the duplicate course. 3\. System recalculates the total price. \- Payment Gateway Timeout/Failure 1\. Payment gateway fails to respond or payment is rejected. 2\. System marks the order as "Failed" or "Cancelled". 3\. System displays an error message and allows the Learner to retry payment. |  |  |
| Priority: | High |  |  |
| Frequency of Use: | Approximately 300 users, average of one usage per day. Peak usage load for this use case is between 9:00 A.M. and 10:00 A.M. local time. |  |  |
| Business Rules: | BR-1. Order total must always be greater than or equal to 0\. BR-2. A pending order automatically expires and cancels after 15 minutes of inactivity. BR-3. Learners cannot purchase a course they have already successfully enrolled in. |  |  |
| Other Information: | 1\. The system should generate a unique Order Reference ID (e.g., ORD-20260525-XYZ). 2\. An automated email containing the order summary is sent to the Learner upon order creation. |  |  |
| Assumptions: | Internet connection and QR scanner are functioning normally. New Course move to leaner list of course |  |  |

#### *b. Business Rules*

None

### 3.2 UC-21\_View Video Content  {#3.2-uc-21_view-video-content}

#### *a. Functional Description*

| ID and Name: | UC-21 View Video Content  |  |  |
| ----: | :---- | ----: | :---- |
| Created By: | HoangCT | Date Created: | 25/5/2026  |
| Primary Actor: | Learner  | Secondary Actors: | Video Streaming Server / Content Delivery Network (CDN)  |
| Description: | Learner can watch video lectures within an enrolled course. The system streams the video content, tracks the Learner's watch progress, and updates the lesson completion status.  |  |  |
| Trigger: | Learner selects a specific video lesson from the course curriculum on the learning dashboard.  |  |  |
| Preconditions: | PRE-1. Learner is logged into the system.  PRE-2. Learner has successfully enrolled in the target course (Order status is "Completed").  PRE-3. The requested lesson is published and accessible.  |  |  |
| Postconditions: | POST-1. Video content is streamed to the Learner's device. POST-2. Learner's viewing timestamp and completion progress are updated in the database. |  |  |
| Normal Flow: | 1\. Learner accesses the course learning interface. 2\. Learner clicks on a video lesson title. 3\. System verifies Learner's enrollment status and access permissions. 4\. System retrieves the video file URL from the Streaming Server. 5\. System loads the video player and related lesson materials (descriptions, resources). 6\. Learner clicks play on the video. 7\. System periodically saves the Learner's watch timestamp (e.g., every 10 seconds). 8\. Learner finishes the video. 9\. System marks the video lesson as "Completed". 10\. System updates the overall course progress bar. |  |  |
| Alternative Flows: | **\- Resume Video Playback** 1\. At step 5, System detects a previously saved watch timestamp for this lesson. 2\. System prompts the Learner "Resume from where you left off?". 3\. Learner accepts, and the video starts playing from the saved timestamp. **\- Adjust Video Quality** 1\. Learner selects the settings gear in the video player. 2\. Learner manually changes the resolution (e.g., 480p, 720p, 1080p). 3\. System streams the selected quality format. |  |  |
| Exceptions: | **\- Access Denied (Not Enrolled)** 1\. System detects the Learner does not own the course. 2\. System blocks access and displays a prompt to purchase the course. **\- Video Source Unavailable** 1\. System fails to connect to the Streaming Server. 2\. System displays an error: "Video source is currently unavailable. Please check your connection or try again later." |  |  |
| Priority: | High |  |  |
| Business Rules: | BR-1. A lesson is only marked as "Completed" automatically if the Learner watches at least 90% of the video duration. BR-2. Learners can replay completed videos an unlimited number of times as long as they have access to the course. BR-3. Video playback tracking must work across different devices for the same user account. |  |  |
| Other Information: | 1\. The video player should support standard controls: Play/Pause, Volume, Speed adjustment (1x, 1.25x, 1.5x), and Fullscreen. 2\. Closed Captions (CC) should be displayed if provided by the Instructor. |  |  |

#### *b. Business Rules*

None

## 3\. Business Rules {#3.-business-rules}

*\[Provide common business rules that you must follow. The information can be provided in the table format as the sample below\]*

 

| ID | Category | Rule Definition |
| ----- | ----- | ----- |
| BR-01 | Security / Auth | User passwords must be hashed using a secure encryption algorithm (e.g., BCrypt) before being stored in the database. |
| BR-02 | Security / Auth | If a user inputs incorrect credentials 6 times consecutively, their account is locked for 30 minutes. |
| BR-03 | Course Management | Course price must be greater than or equal to 0 (free courses are allowed). |
| BR-04 | Course Management | A newly created course must default to **Draft** status and is not visible to learners until approved and published. |
| BR-11 | Course Management | Unregistered Guests and Learners can only view courses that are in **Published** status. |
| BR-12 | Course Management | Instructors can view all of their own courses in any status, but can only browse Published courses of other instructors. |
| BR-13 | Course Management | Managers have complete administrative authority to approve, reject, hide, or moderate any course on the platform. |
| BR-14 | Order / Checkout | The total order value must always be greater than or equal to 0\. If the course is free, no payment order needs to be created; when the learner clicks "buy," the payment step will be skipped, and the learner can own the course. |
| BR-15 | Order / Checkout | A pending order automatically expires and is cancelled after 15 minutes of inactivity, releasing reserved coupon limits. |
| BR-16 | Order / Checkout | Learners cannot purchase or checkout a course they are already successfully enrolled in or own. |
| BR-17 | Course Learning | A video lesson is automatically marked as Completed only if the Learner watches at least 90% of the video duration. |
| BR-18 | Marketing / Coupons | Active coupons must have a valid usage limit or expiration date. A coupon is automatically disabled once it is expired or the limit is reached. |
| BR-19 | Marketing / Coupons | Instructors are only allowed to create and apply discount codes to courses they own. The system allows students to apply multiple discount codes in the same shopping cart/order, provided that: A maximum of 1 discount code per instructor. When applying Instructor A's discount code, the discount amount is calculated only based on Instructor A's courses in the shopping cart. The revenue and selling price of courses belonging to Instructors B, C, etc., remain completely unchanged and are not affected. It is not permitted to combine multiple discount codes from the same instructor on the same course (no stacking). |
| BR-20 | Instructor Registration | Regular users must submit a Personal Profile, CV, and valid teaching certificates to apply for the Instructor role; this request requires manual review by the Manager. |
| BR-21 | Financial Transactions | Financial transaction history cannot be edited or deleted after the payment status has been completed ("Completed" or "Failed") for system auditing purposes. |
| BR-22 | Feedback & Reviews | Students are only allowed to submit reviews for courses they have successfully purchased and enrolled in. |
| BR-23 | Access Restriction | Unenrolled Learners and Guests cannot access the full learning materials or watch locked videos; they can only view the course overview, syllabus, and promotional previews. |
| BR-24 | Status Sync | The system must validate the availability and status of all courses in the cart upon page load. If a course is hidden, deleted, or already owned, it must be automatically removed from the cart. |
